urls.title: Set up the desktop server | Developer Docs
urls.content:
note

We strongly recommend the [remote server](/docs/figma-mcp-server/remote-server-installation/). The desktop server requires the [Figma desktop app](https://www.figma.com/downloads/) and a [Dev or Full seat](https://help.figma.com/hc/en-us/articles/27468498501527-Updates-to-Figma-s-pricing-seats-and-billing-experience#h_01JCPBM8X2MBEXTABDM92HWZG4) on a Professional, Education, Organization, Government, or Enterprise [plan](https://help.figma.com/hc/en-us/articles/360040328273). It doesn't support writing to the canvas or sending UI to Figma.

## Step 1: Enable the desktop server in Figma[​](#step-1 "Direct link to Step 1: Enable the desktop server in Figma")

1.  Open the [Figma desktop app](https://www.figma.com/downloads/) and make sure it’s [up to date](https://help.figma.com/hc/en-us/articles/360039824114-Update-the-Figma-desktop-app).
2.  Create or open a Figma Design file.
3.  With nothing selected, switch to [Dev Mode](https://help.figma.com/hc/en-us/articles/15023124644247-Guide-to-Dev-Mode) using the toggle in the toolbar, or press **Shift** **D**.
4.  In the **MCP server** section of the right sidebar, click **Enable desktop MCP server**.

A confirmation message appears at the bottom of the screen when the server is running. The desktop server runs locally at `http://127.0.0.1:3845/mcp`. You’ll need this address in the next step.

## Step 2: Connect your client[​](#step-2 "Direct link to Step 2: Connect your client")

See the [steps for your client](#client-setup). For other clients, add the server using this configuration:

```
{  "mcpServers": {    "figma-desktop": {      "url": "http://127.0.0.1:3845/mcp"    }  }}
```

Then refresh or restart the server in your client. You should see a successful connection and a list of available tools. If the connection fails or no tools appear, check that the server is still enabled in the Figma desktop app.

## Step 3 (optional): Adjust desktop server settings[​](#step-3 "Direct link to Step 3 (optional): Adjust desktop server settings")

In the **MCP server** section of the right sidebar in Dev Mode, click **Open settings modal**. You can change:

*   **Image settings**: Choose how image assets are handled.
    
    *   **Local server**: Returns localhost links to images, so you can use the actual image assets wherever your file is rendered.
    *   **Download assets**: Lets the MCP server download image assets, such as icons and images, from Figma into your project.
*   **Enable Code Connect**: Includes Code Connect mappings in responses, so generated code can reuse components from your codebase where possible.
    

## Steps for each client[​](#client-setup "Direct link to Steps for each client")

After you [enable the desktop server](#step-1), follow the steps for your client. Xcode supports the remote server only.

### Claude Code[​](#claude-code "Direct link to Claude Code")

1.  In your terminal, run:
    
    ```
    claude mcp add --transport http figma-desktop http://127.0.0.1:3845/mcp
    ```
    
2.  Restart Claude Code so it picks up the change.
    
3.  Type `/mcp` to confirm the Figma MCP server is listed.
    

To manage the server from your terminal:

*   List all servers: `claude mcp list`
*   See details for the Figma server: `claude mcp get figma-desktop`
*   Remove the Figma server: `claude mcp remove figma-desktop`

For more about MCP servers in Claude Code, see [Anthropic’s documentation](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp).

### Codex[​](#codex "Direct link to Codex")

1.  In the lower-left corner of Codex, click **Settings**, then click **Settings** again.
2.  In the left sidebar, click **MCP servers**.
3.  Above the list of servers, click **Add server**.
4.  Change the server type from **STDIO** to **Streamable HTTP**.
5.  In the **Name** field, enter `figma-desktop`.
6.  In the **URL** field, enter `http://127.0.0.1:3845/mcp`.
7.  In the lower-right corner, click **Save**.

You can use the desktop server in Codex while the Figma desktop app is open and the desktop server is on.

### Cursor[​](#cursor "Direct link to Cursor")

1.  Open the command palette:
    
    *   **Mac:** Cmd Shift P
    *   **Windows:** Ctrl Shift P
2.  Search for **Cursor Settings**.
    
3.  Select **Tools & MCP**.
    
4.  Click **Add Custom MCP**.
    
5.  Add this configuration to the file:
    
    ```
    {  "mcpServers": {    "figma-desktop": {      "url": "http://127.0.0.1:3845/mcp"    }  }}
    ```
    
6.  Save the file and go back to **Cursor Settings**.
    

When the Figma MCP server shows as on, you're ready to use the desktop server in Cursor.

### VS Code[​](#vs-code "Direct link to VS Code")

1.  Open the command palette and search for **MCP: Add Server**.
2.  Select **HTTP**.
3.  Paste the server URL `http://127.0.0.1:3845/mcp`, then press Enter.
4.  When asked for a server ID, enter `figma-desktop`, then press Enter.
5.  Choose where to save the server: for all your projects, or only for the current workspace.
6.  Open the chat (Ctrl Cmd I on Mac, or Ctrl Alt I on Windows) and switch to **Agent** mode.
7.  Type `#get_design_context` to check that the Figma MCP server tools are available. If no tools appear, restart the Figma desktop app and VS Code.

For more about MCP servers in VS Code, see [VS Code's documentation](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/agent-customization/mcp-servers).

## Figma for Government[​](#figma-for-government "Direct link to Figma for Government")

[Figma for Government](https://help.figma.com/hc/en-us/articles/22932461365015-Figma-for-Government) supports the desktop server only. To set it up, follow the desktop server steps using the Figma for Government desktop app instead of the standard Figma desktop app.

These tools are available:

*   `get_screenshot`
*   `get_design_context`
*   `get_metadata`
*   `get_figjam`
*   `get_variable_defs`
*   `get_code_connect_map`
*   `add_code_connect_map`
*   `create_design_system_rules`

These features aren't currently available on Figma for Government:

*   The remote MCP server
*   [Writing to the canvas](/docs/figma-mcp-server/write-to-canvas/), including `use_figma`
*   [Sending UI to Figma](/docs/figma-mcp-server/code-to-canvas/), including `generate_figma_design`
*   The Code Connect UI (the [Code Connect CLI](https://developers.figma.com/docs/code-connect/quickstart-guide/) is supported)
*   Agent skills

caution

MCP services for Figma for Government aren't included in Figma’s FedRAMP audit. Figma is working to bring them into scope for a future audit. If you're evaluating Figma for Government against FedRAMP requirements, account for this.

urls.title: Rate limits & access | Developer Docs
urls.content:
## Who can use the MCP server, and what are the rate limits?[​](#rate-limits "Direct link to Who can use the MCP server, and what are the rate limits?")

How often you can use the MCP server depends on your plan and seat. Per-minute limits apply in addition to daily or monthly limits.

Seat

Starter

Professional

Organization

Enterprise

View, Collab

Up to 20 per month

Up to 20 per month

Up to 20 per month

Up to 20 per month

Full, Dev

—

Up to 200 per day, 10 per minute

Up to 200 per day, 15 per minute

Up to 600 per day, 20 per minute

Education plans have the same limits as Full and Dev seats on the Professional plan: up to 200 tool calls per day and 10 per minute.

Rate limits apply to tools that read data from Figma. Some tools are exempt, including tools that write to Figma files, such as:

*   `add_code_connect_map`
*   `create_new_file`
*   `generate_figma_design`
*   `whoami`

Actions that use Figma AI credits, like generating images or sending prompts to Figma Make, don't count toward MCP rate limits.

Figma may change rate limits at any time.

## What can I do if I'm rate limited?[​](#rate-limited "Direct link to What can I do if I'm rate limited?")

You can get higher limits by upgrading your seat or plan:

*   **Starter plan** (20 per month): Upgrade to a Professional, Organization, or Enterprise plan with a Full or Dev seat.
*   **View or Collab seat** (20 per month): Upgrade to a Full or Dev seat.
*   **Full or Dev seat on a Professional, Education, or Organization plan** (200 per day): Upgrade to an Enterprise plan for up to 600 per day.

## Does the MCP server use Figma AI credits?[​](#ai-credits "Direct link to Does the MCP server use Figma AI credits?")

Most MCP server tools don't use [Figma AI credits](https://help.figma.com/hc/en-us/articles/33459875669015). These do:

*   [`generate_image`](/docs/figma-mcp-server/tools-and-prompts/#generate_image) uses credits for each image, like generating an image in Figma Design. The cost depends on the image model.
*   [`send_prompt`](/docs/figma-mcp-server/tools-and-prompts/#send_prompt) uses credits when the Figma Make agent creates or changes code.

Importing a project with `send_code_to_figma` doesn't use credits for the first upload. Prompting and later changes do. Plan, seat, and file permissions still apply.

Figma Weave tools use your Weave credits instead of Figma AI credits.

## Does the MCP server support enterprise-managed authorization?[​](#enterprise-auth "Direct link to Does the MCP server support enterprise-managed authorization?")

Yes, for Claude through Okta Cross App Access (XAA). Usually, each person signs in to Figma separately to use the MCP server. With Okta XAA, members sign in once through Okta, and Claude can then use the Figma MCP server without asking them to sign in again.

Learn how to [set up OIDC for Okta XAA](https://help.figma.com/hc/articles/41992841175959).

## Why am I getting permission errors?[​](#permission-errors "Direct link to Why am I getting permission errors?")

You can only use the MCP server with Figma files you already have access to. If you get an error saying a file or resource can't be accessed:

1.  **Check the link.** Make sure it's a link to a Figma Design, FigJam, or Figma Make file.
2.  **Check which account you're using.** Ask your agent to run `whoami`. It shows the email you're signed in with, your plans, and your seat on each plan.
3.  **Check your access.** Make sure that account belongs to the plan that owns the file.

* * *

urls.title: Create skills for the Figma MCP server | Developer Docs
urls.content:
Who can use this feature

*   Starter, Professional, Education, Organization, and Enterprise [plans](https://help.figma.com/hc/en-us/articles/360040328273)
*   Requires an MCP client that [supports skills](/docs/figma-mcp-server/#h_01K25F7RBRZKCATVJHNXCS6KXW)

Skills package a repeatable Figma workflow into reusable instructions for your agent. Instead of writing long prompts and explaining your conventions every time, a skill gives your agent a consistent set of steps to follow, so results are more reliable from one run to the next.

With the Figma MCP server, custom skills teach your agent to build on your existing design system instead of working around it. A good skill can tell your agent to search your libraries first, use your variable names and modes, and build with your real components and auto layout, following your team’s standards.

For example, you could create a skill to:

*   Move legacy styles or one-off values to variables that follow your library’s structure, including light, dark, or brand modes
*   Create or standardize component sets that match your team’s variant, property, and token conventions
*   Build screens from existing library components, with checks to catch mismatches
*   Run “update and sync” workflows that check what exists, update what changed, and keep design and code aligned

## Set up your skill[​](#set-up "Direct link to Set up your skill")

Each skill is a folder that contains a `SKILL.md` file. Follow the steps for your client:

*   **Claude Code**: In your repository, create a folder at `.claude/skills/<skill-name>/`, then add a `SKILL.md` file to it.
*   **Codex**: In the Codex CLI or app, run `$skill-creator` and follow the prompts. Codex creates the skill folder and `SKILL.md` file for you.
*   **Cursor**: In Cursor chat, run `/create-skill`, describe the skill you want, and follow the prompts. Cursor creates the skill folder and `SKILL.md` file in your workspace.

For other clients, check your client’s documentation for where skills go.

## Write your skill[​](#write "Direct link to Write your skill")

A `SKILL.md` file starts with a short header, called frontmatter, followed by your instructions.

1.  **Name your skill.** In the frontmatter, set `name` to a short identifier in lowercase with hyphens, such as `convert-to-variables`. It should match the skill folder name.
2.  **Describe when to use it.** In the frontmatter, write a `description` that says what the skill does and when to use it. Be specific: “Build a full-page screen using existing library components and variables” works better than “Generate screens.”
3.  **Add a title.** Start the body with a `#` heading that names the workflow, such as `# Generate screen`.
4.  **List when to use it.** Add a `## When to use` section with a few situations where the workflow applies, such as “Creating new screens that must follow an existing design system library.”
5.  **Write numbered steps.** Add an `## Instructions` section with the steps your agent should follow, in order. Write each step as a direct instruction, such as “Search the library first,” “Bind fills, strokes, and text to variables,” or “Prefer semantic tokens.”
6.  **Include an example.** Add an `## Examples` section with at least one sample request and a summary of the expected result, including what gets created or updated.
7.  **Cover edge cases.** Add a `## Common edge cases` section that says what to do when the ideal path fails, such as missing components or tokens, unclear mappings, or unsupported layer types.
8.  **Add other frontmatter only if you need it.** Fields like `compatibility`, `metadata`, or `allowed-tools` are optional. Use them for real requirements, such as needing the Figma MCP server tools, or for ownership and versioning.

### Add supporting files[​](#supporting-files "Direct link to Add supporting files")

As your skills grow, you can add other files to the skill folder. This keeps `SKILL.md` focused on the core steps, while your agent loads the extra files only when it needs them.

*   **Scripts** (`scripts/` folder): Code for steps that are easier, safer, or more consistent to do with code, like transforming data, validating a file before making changes, or checking output for errors. Make scripts self-contained, document any dependencies, and return clear error messages so your agent knows what went wrong.
*   **References** (`references/` folder): Detailed guidance that’s too long for `SKILL.md`, like a naming guide, variable structure, component rules, or a playbook for a specific workflow. Keep each file focused on one topic.
*   **Assets** (`assets/` folder): Reusable materials your agent can read, compare against, or start from, like templates, example files, lookup tables, or a sample of the output structure you want. Assets help keep results consistent across files, teams, and runs.

## Example skill[​](#example "Direct link to Example skill")

This skill creates paint styles from a list of hex color values. It uses `use_figma` and relies on the `figma-use` skill.

Example: figma-apply-palette

```
name: figma-apply-palettedescription: "Creates local paint styles in a Figma file from a list of hex color values. Use when seeding or applying a color palette into Figma from an external list of colors. Does not create color variables or bind to design system tokens — use figma-generate-library for that."compatibility: Requires the figma-use skill to be installed alongside this skillmetadata:  mcp-server: figma# Apply Color Palette — Figma MCP SkillCreates local paint styles in a Figma file from a user-provided list of hex color values using `use_figma`.**Always pass `skillNames: "figma-apply-palette"` when calling `use_figma` as part of this skill.** This is a logging parameter — it does not affect execution.## Prerequisites**You MUST invoke the `figma-use` skill (Skill tool: `skill: "figma-use"`) before every `use_figma` call.** It contains critical Plugin API rules, gotchas, and script templates that prevent hard-to-debug failures. Never call `use_figma` without it.## Skill Boundaries**This skill does:** Create local paint styles from a list of hex values with optional names.**This skill does not:** Create color variables, bind styles to design system tokens, or modify existing styles. For a full design system token workflow, use `figma-generate-library`.If the user asks for something outside these boundaries, say so and suggest what skill or approach would be appropriate.## Workflow### Step 1: Gather inputsAsk the user for:- The Figma file URL or file key to write to- The list of hex values to apply, with optional names (e.g. `Brand/Blue → #3B82F6`)If names are not provided, derive them from the hex value (e.g. `Color/#3B82F6`).### Step 2: Check for existing paint styles (optional)If the user wants to avoid duplicates, or if the file may already have styles, run a read-only inspection first:```js(async () => {  try {    const styles = (await figma.getLocalPaintStylesAsync()).map(s => ({ id: s.id, name: s.name }));    figma.closePlugin(JSON.stringify({ styles }));  } catch(e) { figma.closePluginWithFailure(e.toString()); }})()
```

Skip any colors whose names already exist in the result.

### Step 3: Create paint styles[​](#step-3-create-paint-styles "Direct link to Step 3: Create paint styles")

Create all styles in a single `use_figma` call:

```
(async () => {  try {    const palette = [      { name: "Brand/Blue", hex: "#3B82F6" },      // ... populate from user input    ];    function hexToRgb(hex) {      return {        r: parseInt(hex.slice(1, 3), 16) / 255,        g: parseInt(hex.slice(3, 5), 16) / 255,        b: parseInt(hex.slice(5, 7), 16) / 255,      };    }    const created = [];    for (const { name, hex } of palette) {      const style = figma.createPaintStyle();      style.name = name;      style.paints = [{ type: "SOLID", color: hexToRgb(hex), opacity: 1 }];      created.push({ id: style.id, name: style.name });    }    figma.closePlugin(JSON.stringify({ created }));  } catch(e) { figma.closePluginWithFailure(e.toString()); }})()
```

Confirm with the user how many styles were created.

## Error Recovery[​](#error-recovery "Direct link to Error Recovery")

On any `use_figma` error:

1.  **STOP** — do not immediately retry
2.  Call `get_metadata` to inspect partial state and identify orphaned styles
3.  Remove duplicate or partial styles before retrying
4.  Fix the root cause, then retry

For the full validation workflow, load `figma-use` (Skill tool: `skill: "figma-use"`) and see its validation-and-recovery reference.

```
</details>Start with the core instructions, then add client-specific options only where you need them.## Best practices \{#best-practices}- **Write descriptions like routing rules.** Your agent decides when to use a skill mostly from its `description`. Say when to use it and when not to.- **Keep `SKILL.md` focused.** Move long or specialized details into [supporting files](#supporting-files).- **Make high-risk skills manual only.** For skills that make significant changes, use your client’s option to stop the skill from running automatically, such as `disable-model-invocation`. Check your client’s documentation.## Test your skill \{#test}:::cautionTest new skills on a duplicate or example file, not on a file you depend on.:::To run your skill:- **Claude Code**: Type `/<skill-name>` in the chat.- **Codex**: In the Codex CLI or app, run `/skills` or type `$`, then select your skill.- **Cursor**: In Agent chat, type `/` and select your skill, or type `/<skill-name>`.## Find and share skills \{#share}Browse skills from other teams in the [Figma Community](https://www.figma.com/community/skills) and the [Figma community-resources repo](https://github.com/figma/community-resources/tree/main/agent_skills) on GitHub.
```

urls.title: Code Connect integration | Developer Docs
urls.content:
When your design system components are connected to code with Code Connect, the Figma MCP server adds real implementation details from your codebase to the context it sends your agent. This helps your agent generate code that uses your actual components and follows your team's patterns.

For an overview of Code Connect and how to set it up, see [Code Connect](https://help.figma.com/hc/en-us/articles/23920389749655-Code-Connect).

## What your agent gets from Code Connect[​](#what-your-agent-gets "Direct link to What your agent gets from Code Connect")

When the MCP server processes a frame that contains connected components, it wraps each one in a `<CodeConnectSnippet>` marker in the context it sends your agent. Each marker can include:

*   **Design properties**: The component's current property values in Figma, such as variants, boolean properties, and text
*   **Import statements**: How to import the component in your code
*   **Component snippet**: Code showing how to use the component
*   **Instructions**: Any [custom instructions](#custom-instructions) you've added to guide your agent

What's inside each marker depends on whether you set up the connection with Code Connect CLI or Code Connect UI.

Code Connect CLI

Code Connect UI

**Import statement**

Uses the `imports` field in your Code Connect file. If that's empty, uses the `source` field, which is filled in automatically in some cases, such as React. If both are empty, there's no import statement.

Generated from the component path and component name you entered for the connection. If you didn't enter a component name, it's based on the Figma component's name.

**Component snippet**

The snippets you wrote in your Code Connect file, including how Figma properties map to your component's props and where the component is defined

Generated from the Figma component's name and current properties. Shows which component to use and basic usage, but not full code snippets.

**Best for**

Detailed, exact examples of how your team uses each component

Quick setup inside Figma, with [custom instructions](#custom-instructions) for extra guidance

## Add custom instructions[​](#custom-instructions "Direct link to Add custom instructions")

With Code Connect UI, you can add instructions to each connection to give your agent more guidance, such as prop patterns, accessibility requirements, and team conventions. The MCP server includes them in the marker as user rules.

To add instructions, use **Add instructions for MCP** when you set up or edit a connection. Learn how in the [Code Connect UI setup guide](https://developers.figma.com/docs/code-connect/code-connect-ui-setup/#add-instructions-for-ai-code-generation).

## Choose which framework your agent gets[​](#multiple-frameworks "Direct link to Choose which framework your agent gets")

If a component is connected to more than one framework, such as React and SwiftUI, you can control which connection your agent receives:

*   **Desktop server**: Uses the Code Connect connection you've selected in Dev Mode.
*   **Remote server**: Ask your agent to set the `clientFrameworks` parameter to your Code Connect label, such as `React` or `SwiftUI`.

note

On Professional plans, the MCP server only returns connections for your active library and framework.

## Best practices[​](#best-practices "Direct link to Best practices")

*   **Start with your core components.** Connect the components your team uses most first.
*   **Add custom instructions.** Document component-specific patterns, accessibility requirements, and edge cases.
*   **Keep connections up to date.** When a component's API changes in your codebase, update its Code Connect connection.
*   **Test and refine your instructions.** Use the preview in Code Connect UI to check the generated snippets, and adjust your instructions until they match your team's patterns.

*   [Code Connect](https://help.figma.com/hc/en-us/articles/23920389749655-Code-Connect)
*   [Get started with Code Connect CLI](https://developers.figma.com/docs/code-connect/quickstart-guide/)
*   [Get started with Code Connect UI](https://developers.figma.com/docs/code-connect/code-connect-ui-setup/)
*   [Add custom rules for the Figma MCP server](/docs/figma-mcp-server/add-custom-rules/)
